Lia: Heads up — restore times for tenant-42 jumped ~6x after last night's per-tenant CMK rollout. Not yet a customer-impact alert but hitting our restore SLOs in staging. Can we triage?
Sam: :eyes: saw this in the SRE dashboards, CPU on the restore workers spiked and I saw repeated KMS Deny errors in the logs around 03:12 UTC.
Maya: I ran a local canary — when KV decryption fails we fall back to server-side re-encrypt flow which serializes and re-chunks blobs, that path is much heavier.
Kevin: Any RBAC or grant changes around the uploader/restore role? We did a small IAM tidy-up yesterday.
Lia: Yes — security rotated the uploader role and tightened grants. I pushed the policy change at 02:50 to remove broad kms:Decrypt for the legacy service account that used to be allowed.
backup-bot: [automated] snapshot-restore-canoary tenant-42: started 03:05 UTC, duration 00:04:22, result: slow-path (re-encrypt fallback)
Sam: Logs show repeated KMS::AccessDenied for the object-uploader SA:
```
ERROR backup/restore.go: decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: user does not have kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd
```
Maya: So the uploader can't use the tenant CMK and the restore path decrypts with a cluster key then re-encrypts with the tenant key again which causes high IO and CPU.
Lia: That matches. Impact: longer restores + queueing which increases tail latency for live failovers.
Oncall-Eng: Should we temporarily pin the restore service to the cluster CMK to avoid the fallback while we fix grants? That would reduce isolation but restore SLOs would be met.
Kevin: If we pin to cluster CMK we need an audit log entry and a short-lived exception. Also must notify compliance.
Sam: Quick mitigation plan: 1) Re-add kms:Decrypt grant for uploader SA scoped to the tenant CMKs (least privilege) 2) Re-run the failing canary 3) If still slow, pin service to cluster CMK as short-lived fallback 4) Run postmortem and tighten rollout guardrails.
Lia: I can re-add the grant now — will scope by resource (tenant-42 key) and set an expiration 24h. Will post the exact IAM diff here before applying.
Maya: After grant is back, we should run these checks: a) run 10 concurrent canaries b) check restore worker CPU and queue length c) validate no AccessDenied artifacts in audit logs.
Kevin: Policy diff please. Also add a guard in the deploy pipeline: any CMK-per-tenant rollout must have a preflight RBAC test that simulates restores.
Lia: Pushing policy diff (preview):
```
- Resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:acct:key/tenant-42
  Effect: Deny
+ Resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:acct:key/tenant-42
  Action: kms:Decrypt
  Effect: Allow
  Principal: serviceAccount:object-uploader@prod
  Condition: {"DateLessThan": {"aws:CurrentTime":"2026-03-22T03:12:00Z"}}
```
Lia: Applying now.
backup-bot: [automated] iam-change detected by encops on 03:28 UTC — grant added for object-uploader to tenant-42 CMK (expires 2026-03-22T03:12:00Z)
Sam: Re-running canary...
backup-bot: [automated] snapshot-restore-canoary tenant-42: started 03:33 UTC, duration 00:00:58, result: fast-path
Maya: Nice — CPU back to baseline, no re-encrypt fallback in traces.
Oncall-Eng: Good. Action items: Lia to open a short-lived exception ticket (security) and notify compliance; Kevin to add preflight RBAC test to the CMK rollout job; Maya to add a metric alert for KMS AccessDenied spikes; Sam to run a broader runbook sweep for other tenants.
Lia: Filing the exception & compliance notification now. I'll also add a follow-up note on the rollout checklist: add canary restore and audit log verification.
Kevin: One more thing — please record which deploy removed the grants; we need to update our deploy-owner runbook so future RBAC tidy-ups run preflight checks.
Lia: Will include deploy id and PR link in the postmortem. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
